title: महँगी, बेरोजगारी र राजनीतिक विवादले तात्यो युरोप- हजारौँ सडकमा उत्रिए
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । बढ्दो महँगी, आवास समस्या, सार्वजनिक सेवाको अवस्था र राजनीतिक विवादलाई लिएर युरोपका विभिन्न प्रमुख सहरमा विरोध प्रदर्शन भएका छन् । सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत प्रदर्शनका लागि आह्वान गरिएपछि विभिन्न देशमा प्रहरीले सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारेको छ । फ्रान्सको गृह मन्त्रालयका अनुसार शनिबार देशभर भएका प्रदर्शनमा करिब तीन लाख २० हजार मानिस सहभागी भए । तीमध्ये ७० हजार पेरिसमा थिए । आयोजकहरूले भने देशभर पाँच लाख र राजधानीमा दुई लाख मानिस सहभागी भएको दाबी गरेका छन् । प्रदर्शनलाई ध्यानमा राख्दै देशभर करिब ७० हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी परिचालन गरिएको थियो । अधिकांश प्रदर्शन शान्तिपूर्ण भए पनि केही स्थानमा प्रहरीसँग झडप भएको थियो । फ्रान्सका गृहमन्त्री लरेन्ट नुनेजका अनुसार प्रदर्शनका क्रममा ४२२ जना पक्राउ परेका छन् । जर्मनीका ३० भन्दा बढी सहरमा भएका प्रदर्शनमा सार्वजनिक सेवामा लगानी बढाउन, महँगी नियन्त्रण गर्न र अनिवार्य सैन्य सेवाको व्यवस्था हटाउन माग गरिएको थियो । आयोजकहरूका अनुसार १२ सहरको तथ्याङ्कमा मात्रै ६८ हजारभन्दा बढी सहभागी भएका थिए । फ्र्याङ्कफर्टमा प्रहरी अधिकारी घाइते भएका थिए भने ह्याम्बर्गमा अवरोधका लागि राखिएका बारमा आगजनी गरिएको थियो । ब्रेमेनमा पनि प्रहरीमाथि आक्रमण भएको जर्मन समाचार संस्था डीपीएले जनाएको छ । इटालीमा सार्वजनिक सेवा र जीवनयापनको खर्चलाई लिएर शुक्रबार ६० भन्दा बढी सहरमा प्रदर्शन भएका थिए । युनियनको अनुमानमा १५ लाख मानिस सहभागी भए पनि गृह मन्त्रालयले सहभागी सङ्ख्या दुई लाख ५५ हजार रहेको जनाएको छ । शनिबार पनि रोमस्थित कोलोसियम नजिक प्रदर्शनकारी भेला भएका थिए । पोर्चुगलको लिस्बन र पोर्टोमा आवासको समस्या समाधान गर्न माग गर्दै एक हजारभन्दा बढी मानिसले प्रदर्शन गरेका थिए । लिस्बनमा प्रदर्शनकारीले रोसियो स्क्वायरमा रात बिताउने तयारी गरेका थिए । यसैबीच, अल्बानियाको राजधानी तिरानामा प्रधानमन्त्री एदी रामाको राजीनामालगायत माग राखेर भइरहेको प्रदर्शन शनिबार १९औँ दिन पनि जारी रह्यो । प्रदर्शनका क्रममा प्रहरीमाथि पेट्रोल बम र ढुङ्गा प्रहार भएपछि प्रहरीले अश्रुग्यास र पानीको फोहोरा प्रयोग गरेको थियो । पोल्याण्डको वार्सामा संवैधानिक न्यायाधिकरणको संरचना र नेतृत्वलाई लिएर प्रदर्शन भएको थियो । यता नेदरल्याण्ड्सको द हेगमा सामाजिक सञ्जालबाट भएको आह्वानपछि भेला भएका भीडलाई प्रहरीले तितरबितर पारेको थियो । प्रहरीले दिनभर ३४ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ । स्पेनको म्याड्रिड, बार्सिलोना र भ्यालेन्सियामा पनि सम्भावित अशान्ति रोक्न सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारिएको थियो । अघिल्लो सप्ताहन्त बार्सिलोनामा भएको झडपमा १५ प्रहरी अधिकारी घाइते भएका र १२८ जना पक्राउ परेका थिए । स्पेनी समाचार संस्था ईएफईका अनुसार अनलाइनमार्फत हिंसा भड्काएको आशङ्कामा प्रहरीले देशभर १० जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको थियो । Kathmandu. Protests have taken place in major cities across Europe over rising inflation, housing problems, the state of public services and political disputes. Police in various countries have tightened security following calls for demonstrations on social media. According to the French Interior Ministry, about 320,000 people took part in the demonstrations across the country on Saturday. Of these, 70,000 were in Paris. Organizers claimed that 500,000 people took part across the country and 200,000 in the capital. Around 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country in view of the protests. Although most of the demonstrations were peaceful, there were clashes with police in some places. According to French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, 422 people were arrested during the protests. The demonstrations in more than 30 German cities called for increased investment in public services, price controls and the abolition of compulsory military service. Organizers said more than 68,000 people took part in the 12 cities alone. A police officer was injured in Frankfurt, while a barricade was set on fire in Hamburg. Police were also attacked in Bremen, German news agency DPA reported. Protests in more than 60 cities across Italy on Friday over public services and the cost of living. Unions estimated that 1.5 million people took part, while the Interior Ministry put the number at 255,000. Protesters also gathered near the Colosseum in Rome on Saturday. More than 1,000 people demonstrated in Lisbon and Porto, Portugal, demanding a solution to the housing crisis. In Lisbon, protesters were preparing to spend the night in Rossio Square. Meanwhile, protests in the Albanian capital Tirana, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, continued for the 19th day on Saturday. Police used tear gas and water cannons after petrol bombs and stones were thrown at them during the demonstration. In Warsaw, Poland, there was a demonstration against the structure and leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal. Meanwhile, in The Hague, Netherlands, police dispersed a crowd that had gathered after a call on social media. Police said they arrested 34 people throughout the day. Security was also tightened in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia in Spain to prevent possible unrest. Clashes in Barcelona last weekend left 15 police officers injured and 128 people arrested. According to Spanish news agency EFE, police arrested 10 people across the country on suspicion of inciting violence online.

रोसियो स्क्वायरमा रात बिताउने तयारी गरेका थिए । यसैबीच, अल्बानियाको राजधानी तिरानामा प्रधानमन्त्री एदी रामाको राजीनामालगायत माग राखेर भइरहेको प्रदर्शन शनिबार १९औँ दिन पनि जारी रह्यो । प्रदर्शनका क्रममा प्रहरीमाथि पेट्रोल बम र ढुङ्गा प्रहार भएपछि प्रहरीले अश्रुग्यास र पानीको फोहोरा प्रयोग गरेको थियो । पोल्याण्डको वार्सामा संवैधानिक न्यायाधिकरणको संरचना र नेतृत्वलाई लिएर प्रदर्शन भएको थियो । यता नेदरल्याण्ड्सको द हेगमा सामाजिक सञ्जालबाट भएको आह्वानपछि भेला भएका भीडलाई प्रहरीले तितरबितर पारेको थियो । प्रहरीले दिनभर ३४ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ । स्पेनको म्याड्रिड, बार्सिलोना र भ्यालेन्सियामा पनि सम्भावित अशान्ति रोक्न सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारिएको थियो । अघिल्लो सप्ताहन्त बार्सिलोनामा भएको झडपमा १५ प्रहरी अधिकारी घाइते भएका र १२८ जना पक्राउ परेका थिए । स्पेनी समाचार संस्था ईएफईका अनुसार अनलाइनमार्फत हिंसा भड्काएको आशङ्कामा प्रहरीले देशभर १० जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको थियो । Kathmandu. Protests have taken place in major cities across Europe over rising inflation, housing problems, the state of public services and political disputes. Police in various countries have tightened security following calls for demonstrations on social media. According to the French Interior Ministry, about 320,000 people took part in the demonstrations across the country on Saturday. Of these, 70,000 were in Paris. Organizers claimed that 500,000 people took part across the country and 200,000 in the capital. Around 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country in view of the protests. Although most of the demonstrations were peaceful, there were clashes with police in some places. According to French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, 422 people were arrested during the protests. The demonstrations in more than 30 German cities called for increased investment in public services, price controls and the abolition of compulsory military service. Organizers said more than 68,000 people took part in the 12 cities alone. A police officer was injured in Frankfurt, while a barricade was set on fire in Hamburg. Police were also attacked in Bremen, German news agency DPA reported. Protests in more than 60 cities across Italy on Friday over public services and the cost of living. Unions estimated that 1.5 million people took part, while the Interior Ministry put the number at 255,000. Protesters also gathered near the Colosseum in Rome on Saturday. More than 1,000 people demonstrated in Lisbon and Porto, Portugal, demanding a solution to the housing crisis. In Lisbon, protesters were preparing to spend the night in Rossio Square. Meanwhile, protests in the Albanian capital Tirana, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, continued for the 19th day on Saturday. Police used tear gas and water cannons after petrol bombs and stones were thrown at them during the demonstration. In Warsaw, Poland, there was a demonstration against the structure and leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal. Meanwhile, in The Hague, Netherlands, police dispersed a crowd that had gathered after a call on social media. Police said they arrested 34 people throughout the day. Security was also tightened in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia in Spain to prevent possible unrest. Clashes in Barcelona last weekend left 15 police officers injured and 128 people arrested. According to Spanish news agency EFE, police arrested 10 people across the country on suspicion of inciting violence online.

काठमाडौं । बढ्दो महँगी, आवास समस्या, सार्वजनिक सेवाको अवस्था र राजनीतिक विवादलाई लिएर युरोपका विभिन्न प्रमुख सहरमा विरोध प्रदर्शन भएका छन् । सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत प्रदर्शनका लागि आह्वान गरिएपछि विभिन्न देशमा प्रहरीले सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारेको छ । फ्रान्सको गृह मन्त्रालयका अनुसार शनिबार देशभर भएका प्रदर्शनमा करिब तीन लाख २० हजार मानिस सहभागी भए । तीमध्ये ७० हजार पेरिसमा थिए । आयोजकहरूले भने देशभर पाँच लाख र राजधानीमा दुई लाख मानिस सहभागी भएको दाबी गरेका छन् । प्रदर्शनलाई ध्यानमा राख्दै देशभर करिब ७० हजार सुरक्षाकर्मी परिचालन गरिएको थियो । अधिकांश प्रदर्शन शान्तिपूर्ण भए पनि केही स्थानमा प्रहरीसँग झडप भएको थियो । फ्रान्सका गृहमन्त्री लरेन्ट नुनेजका अनुसार प्रदर्शनका क्रममा ४२२ जना पक्राउ परेका छन् । जर्मनीका ३० भन्दा बढी सहरमा भएका प्रदर्शनमा सार्वजनिक सेवामा लगानी बढाउन, महँगी नियन्त्रण गर्न र अनिवार्य सैन्य सेवाको व्यवस्था हटाउन माग गरिएको थियो । आयोजकहरूका अनुसार १२ सहरको तथ्याङ्कमा मात्रै ६८ हजारभन्दा बढी सहभागी भएका थिए । फ्र्याङ्कफर्टमा प्रहरी अधिकारी घाइते भएका थिए भने ह्याम्बर्गमा अवरोधका लागि राखिएका बारमा आगजनी गरिएको थियो । ब्रेमेनमा पनि प्रहरीमाथि आक्रमण भएको जर्मन समाचार संस्था डीपीएले जनाएको छ । इटालीमा सार्वजनिक सेवा र जीवनयापनको खर्चलाई लिएर शुक्रबार ६० भन्दा बढी सहरमा प्रदर्शन भएका थिए । युनियनको अनुमानमा १५ लाख मानिस सहभागी भए पनि गृह मन्त्रालयले सहभागी सङ्ख्या दुई लाख ५५ हजार रहेको जनाएको छ । शनिबार पनि रोमस्थित कोलोसियम नजिक प्रदर्शनकारी भेला भएका थिए । पोर्चुगलको लिस्बन र पोर्टोमा आवासको समस्या समाधान गर्न माग गर्दै एक हजारभन्दा बढी मानिसले प्रदर्शन गरेका थिए । लिस्बनमा प्रदर्शनकारीले रोसियो स्क्वायरमा रात बिताउने तयारी गरेका थिए । प्रहरीले अश्रुग्यास र पानीको फोहोरा प्रयोग गरेको थियो । पोल्याण्डको वार्सामा संवैधानिक न्यायाधिकरणको संरचना र नेतृत्वलाई लिएर प्रदर्शन भएको थियो । यता नेदरल्याण्ड्सको द हेगमा सामाजिक सञ्जालबाट भएको आह्वानपछि भेला भएका भीडलाई प्रहरीले तितरबितर पारेको थियो । प्रहरीले दिनभर ३४ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको जनाएको छ । स्पेनको म्याड्रिड, बार्सिलोना र भ्यालेन्सियामा पनि सम्भावित अशान्ति रोक्न सुरक्षा व्यवस्था कडा पारिएको थियो । अघिल्लो सप्ताहन्त बार्सिलोनामा भएको झडपमा १५ प्रहरी अधिकारी घाइते भएका र १२८ जना पक्राउ परेका थिए । स्पेनी समाचार संस्था ईएफईका अनुसार अनलाइनमार्फत हिंसा भड्काएको आशङ्कामा प्रहरीले Kathmandu. Protests have taken place in major cities across Europe over rising inflation, housing problems, the state of public services and political disputes. Police in various countries have tightened security following calls for demonstrations on social media. According to the French Interior Ministry, about 320,000 people took part in the demonstrations across the country on Saturday. Of these, 70,000 were in Paris. Organizers claimed that 500,000 people took part across the country and 200,000 in the capital. Around 70,000 security personnel were deployed across the country in view of the protests. Although most of the demonstrations were peaceful, there were clashes with police in some places. According to French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, 422 people were arrested during the protests. The demonstrations in more than 30 German cities called for increased investment in public services, price controls and the abolition of compulsory military service. Organizers said more than 68,000 people took part in the 12 cities alone. A police officer was injured in Frankfurt, while a barricade was set on fire in Hamburg. Police were also attacked in Bremen, German news agency DPA reported. Protests in more than 60 cities across Italy on Friday over public services and the cost of living. Unions estimated that 1.5 million people took part, while the Interior Ministry put the number at 255,000. Protesters also gathered near the Colosseum in Rome on Saturday. More than 1,000 people demonstrated in Lisbon and Porto, Portugal, demanding a solution to the housing crisis. In Lisbon, protesters were preparing to spend the night in Rossio Square. Meanwhile, protests in the Albanian capital Tirana, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, continued for the 19th day on Saturday. Police used tear gas and water cannons after petrol bombs and stones were thrown at them during the demonstration. In Warsaw, Poland, there was a demonstration against the structure and leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal. Meanwhile, in The Hague, Netherlands, police dispersed a crowd that had gathered after a call on social media. Police said they arrested 34 people throughout the day. Security was also tightened in Madrid, Barcelona and Valencia in Spain to prevent possible unrest. Clashes in Barcelona last weekend left 15 police officers injured and 128 people arrested. According to Spanish news agency EFE, police arrested 10 people across the country on suspicion of inciting violence online.
